comment: Ambient talk for Dustline and Frontier Road east (2026-10-09). Keys are the stable ids on the floors' workers (tools/author_dustline.py); E opens one random line per conversation. Dustline's voice: everything has a price, nobody is what they seem. Services (trade, repair, contracts, lodging) are not implemented yet: lines point at them in-world without promising mechanics. Lore stays provisional: docs/design/DUSTLINE.md.

npc.dustline_gate_guard.name: VOSS  ·  GATE GUARD
lines: Walk in slow, hands where I can see them. Dustline's open to anyone who can pay for the privilege.
Entry's free today. Leaving costs what you owe. Remember that.
Market's straight down Gate Road. If you get lost, look for the tower — the Exchange always knows where you are.
We don't care who you were before the road. We care what you're carrying.
Raiders watch the last stretch of Frontier Road. If you made it this far, they let you. Ask yourself why.

npc.dustline_inspector.name: MARGO  ·  CARGO INSPECTOR
lines: Everything that comes through gets weighed. Everything that's weighed gets taxed.
Declare it or lose it. Your choice, but only one of those is cheap.
Ore, scrap, relics, people. Don't look at me like that — I only write down what the scale says.
That caravan's been 'about to leave' for three days. Somebody's waiting on a better price.
Smuggling's a crime here. Getting caught smuggling is the expensive part.

npc.dustline_caravan_master.name: OLD TALLOW  ·  CARAVAN MASTER
lines: Saltpan, the Scarp, back down to the Outpost. That's the only route I'd sell you a seat on today.
The Floodlands road washed out. East Gate stays shut until somebody pays to dig it clear.
Escorts earn more than haulers and die more often. The board in the market has both kinds of work.
A caravan is a promise with wheels. Most of them break somewhere between here and the shaft.
Every map on that board is wrong somewhere. Mine are wrong in fewer places. That's why they cost more.

npc.dustline_caravaneer.name: PIKE  ·  CARAVANEER
lines: Load, unload, load again. Tallow says we leave at dawn. He said that yesterday too.
You want a lift? Find your own wheels or pay for a seat. Nobody rides free in Dustline.
Heard the Sump's crawling again. We'll take the long way. Long way's still alive.
This crate is heavier than it says on the manifest. I don't ask. You shouldn't either.

npc.dustline_trader_food.name: AUNTIE RHEA  ·  FOOD & WATER
lines: Water's clean, mostly. Rations are dry, always. Price depends on how thirsty you look.
Shelves fill up when the caravans come in. Come back with coin and I'll have something worth it.
You came up from the Outpost? Then you've never eaten anything that grew in daylight. Neither have I.
Haggle all you like, dear. I've been doing this longer than you've been breathing dust.
Everything has a price. Bread just happens to be one most people can afford.

npc.dustline_trader_ammo.name: CASSO  ·  AMMUNITION
lines: Rounds, cells, charges. I don't sell guns — guns are opinions. I sell the arguments.
Stock's thin till the next haul. Whatever you're shooting at, shoot it less.
Count your shots on Frontier Road. Scavengers count theirs.
No credit. Credit is a bullet you hand back to someone who might not return it.
If you see a crate marked with a red stripe on the road, it's mine. Bring it back and we'll talk price.

npc.dustline_trader_meds.name: DOC IVES  ·  MEDICAL
lines: Stims, gauze, filters for your lungs. Dust out here gets in deeper than any blade.
I patch anyone who pays. Who they were fighting is none of my business.
Supplies are short. If you find sealed medical crates below, I pay better than the Exchange.
Don't tell me where it hurts. Tell me what you can spend.
Half of what's sold as medicine in this town is chalk. Mine's only a quarter chalk.

npc.dustline_trader_general.name: SAM  ·  BUYS ANYTHING
lines: I buy what you dragged up and sell it to the next fool who needs it. Margins are the whole religion.
Bring me salvage, relics, ore — I'll name a number. You'll hate it. You'll take it.
Scrap goes to Nell down the Row; she pays by weight. I pay by how badly someone else wants it.
Everybody in Dustline is a trader. Some of us just admit it.
Prices change when the caravans arrive. Sell before they do.

npc.dustline_board_keeper.name: LISTER  ·  CONTRACT BOARD
lines: Hauls, bounties, escorts. Read the board, pick a paper, don't come back empty-handed.
No contracts posted for newcomers yet. The Exchange decides who's worth paying.
Somebody wants a crate brought back from the Saltpan convoy. Somebody else wants it to stay lost.
Bounty on the raiders by the salt works. Pays in coin, not in thanks.
I don't write the jobs. I just pin them up and take a cut. Everyone takes a cut.

npc.dustline_exchange_clerk.name: MS. ORREL  ·  EXCHANGE CLERK
lines: The terminal stores what you can't carry. Same depot as the Outpost booth — the network is the network.
Coin exchange opens when the vaults are counted. They are always being counted.
The Exchange doesn't take sides. It takes deposits.
Your goods are safe with us. Your reasons are your own problem.
Look up. The lantern on the tower never goes out. That's the only promise we make for free.

npc.dustline_smith.name: BRACK  ·  SMITH
lines: Forge isn't taking repair jobs yet — I'm rebuilding the press. Come back when the sparks are steady.
Bring me scrap and I'll make it something. Bring me coin and I'll make it something good.
That drill of yours is held together by luck. Luck's the one alloy I can't weld.
Crafting bench'll be open soon. Until then, keep your gear oiled and your edges dry.
Everything breaks out here. My trade is making it break later.

npc.dustline_scrap_buyer.name: NELL  ·  SCRAP BUYER
lines: Scrap by the kilo, any condition. Rust weighs the same as steel, which is why I love it.
Scales are honest. Mostly. Bring more and they get friendlier.
The convoy on the Saltpan is picked half clean. Half isn't all.
I'll take components, plating, cable, anything with a bolt in it. Not bodies. Not anymore.
That crane over there pulled half this city out of the dirt. Now it pulls the other half apart.

npc.dustline_east_guard.name: EAST GATE GUARD
lines: Gate's shut. Floodlands road washed out and nobody's paid to clear it.
Past this gate it's water, mud and things that like both. Be glad it's closed.
When it opens, it'll cost you. Everything opens for a price.
Caravans bound east wait in the Yard. They've been waiting a while.

npc.dustline_warren_watch.name: WARREN WATCH
lines: Warrens are closed. Exchange orders. Don't ask me which order, there are a lot of them.
Cheap rooms, cheaper questions, people who left the light behind. Not today.
You hear the music down there? Neither do I. Move along.
When the stair opens you'll find beds, a fence or two, and rumours worth more than they cost.
Everything has a price. Down there, sometimes it's you.

npc.dustline_townsfolk_a.name: DUST-EATER
lines: First time in the city? You can tell by how often you look up.
The tower lamp's how you find your way home. Nobody here has a home, but it works anyway.
Don't trust anyone selling maps of the Deep. Trust the ones selling rope.
I sold my boots last winter. Bought them back in spring. Same boots, twice the price.

npc.dustline_townsfolk_b.name: PORTER
lines: Can't stop, crate's due at the Exchange. Everything's due at the Exchange.
Pay's bad, back's worse, but the market never runs out of things to carry.
You want something moved, I'm cheap. You want it moved quietly, I'm not.
Watch your pockets near the stalls. Not everyone sells with their hands out front.

npc.frontier_waystation_keeper.name: HARL  ·  WAYSTATION
lines: Water's free at my fire. Shade too. News costs extra.
Dustline's past the wrecks, straight on. You'll see the wall before you see the city.
Scavengers took the old convoy by the pylons. Go around, or go through quick.
Caravans stop here to wait out the heat. Some never get going again.
The relay pylons still hum at night. Nobody knows who's listening.

npc.frontier_caravan_guard.name: CARAVAN GUARD
lines: Keep walking, friend. This load's spoken for.
We hold the road till dawn, then roll for Dustline. Want to tag along? Bring a rifle.
Castoffs hit the wrecks east of here yesterday. Three of them, maybe more.
Out here, everything's a trade. Even safe passage.

npc.dustline_weapons_merchant.name: RASK  ·  WEAPONS MERCHANT
lines: Rifles, blades, a launcher if you ask nicely. Not today, though. Today I'm only showing.
Stock's still on the road behind me. When it lands, you'll want to be first in line — and carrying coin.
Everything in this car shoots, cuts or burns. Everything has a price. Mine's just higher.
Don't touch the railgun. You can't afford to look at it twice.
Come back when the Exchange lets me open the back of this thing. Weapons, soon. Talk is free.
